name: Hermes Agent
prerequisites: hermes >=0.19.0 installed and on PATH (git install, pipx, or the install script); the CLI is a Python console script, so the binary is a shim into <HERMES_HOME>/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes
an inference provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml (model.default + model.provider) with credentials in <HERMES_HOME>/.env or auth.json — e.g. 'hermes setup' or 'hermes login'
HERMES_HOME exported to the recording home, so the run writes to an isolated state.db instead of the maintainer's real session store
the sqlite3 CLI on PATH — hermes persists no transcript file, so the driver reads session id and turn-completion straight out of state.db

LIVE TOOL ROSTER — BACKEND-GATED, RE-PROBE EVERY RUN (measured both ways 2026-08-03, hermes 0.19.0, HERMES_HOME=/tmp/irr-hermes-home/.hermes): terminal, read_file, write_file, patch, search_files and execute_code are NOT missing from hermes and are NOT unconditionally present — they are gated by `terminal.backend: docker` in the recording home config.yaml. tools/terminal_tool.py::check_terminal_requirements() shells out to `docker version` for the docker backend, and tools/__init__.py::check_file_requirements gates the file toolset the same way, so the whole terminal+file set is callable ONLY while the Docker daemon is running. Measured: 43 callable tools with Docker UP (check_terminal_requirements() returns True); 36 with it DOWN (loader logs "check_fn check_terminal_requirements returned False" and "check_fn _check_file_reqs returned False"). Setting terminal.backend: local also restores them but hands the live agent host shell access — a maintainer decision, not a recorder one. ALWAYS re-probe the roster at the start of a recording instead of trusting a cached list (three recordings were burned on a stale one); probe by importing model_tools.get_tool_definitions() from the install tree with HERMES_HOME pointed at the recording home. skills_list/skill_view are backend-independent and always callable.

TIMING: prefer WIDE generations (e.g. a 30-line count plus two sentences of prose). The store watcher polls every 2s with a 500ms debounce, so a ~1s turn can commit its inbound user row and its assistant finish_reason='stop' row inside a SINGLE scan — the ready→working edge then never exists and any tN_start phase fails. Observed margins on the 2026-08-03 sweep: widened turns gave 1.7s–5.4s working spans, i.e. barely more than one scan gap at the low end. Widen the generation; never weaken the spec.
